finding: Approval identities remain plaintext and can evade erasure reporting
evidence: Reproduced first over HTTP+JSON into a SQLite file: the old code stored "reviewFor":"bearer:alice-n01" and "approvedBy":["bearer:bob-n01"] in the clear, and erasure reported in_clear = [] for a reviewFor subject. One classification (audit/privacy/fields.rs) now drives key resolution, sealing, reveal and the in-clear scan; a source scan fails on any detail key in no list. Live (Qwen3-1.7B, llama.cpp 9daa0aa): an approved tool call's audit file named neither person.
tests: tests/audit_privacy_approvals.rs; audit/privacy unit tests; tests/tool_loop_audit_live.rs (ignored: needs llama-server)

finding: Approved tools can run without the required durable action audit; healthy records say deny
evidence: Reproduced first: with the audit store down after parking, the approved call ran with no record; with a healthy store its record said deny. ToolPolicy::approved is called after the digest check, immediately before invocation; AuditedPolicy writes approval_required (pending) and approved (durable, approvedBy sealed). Live: decisions [approval_required, approval_required, approved] in 8 of 8 runs.

finding: Cross-replica key cleanup can erase a fresh audit record's identity key
note: Fenced in each shipped store; a third-party AuditStore that keeps the trait's defaults is not atomic across processes, as documented.
evidence: Reproduced first with two logs over one store, one paused at the race: on memory, two SQLite pools and two PostgreSQL pools, all six cases failed on the old code (an unrevealable actor; keys deleted under a hold). append_next_naming, delete_subject_key_unless_named and delete_subject_keys_unless_held fence them; all pass now.

finding: Journal clear is unfenced and occurs before final-result publication
evidence: Reproduced first: a stale invocation published its answer and the newer checkpoint was gone; a replay after completion asked the model again. A final answer is a completed checkpoint under the revision fence; replay returns it without model or tool; clear takes a revision; sweep deletes on schedule. Live: a finished run replayed with 0 model calls and 0 tool calls.

finding: Failed terminal repair can delete its only retry marker
evidence: Reproduced first: each of four one-shot faults (task read, log read, log append, configs unreadable) released the reaper's claim. The claim is now kept (TurnClaim::keep_for_repair) until the ending is durable; each fault is repaired on the next look.

finding: Outbox helper returns durable success when recording failed
evidence: record_now returns Option<Recorded> (Durable, NoSubscribers, ConfigsUnread, FromMemory). Reproduced first: the processor logged an ending whose webhooks were never queued; now the ending is not logged and the claim is kept.

finding: Durable checkpoints form a separate plaintext store outside erasure, without tenant/subject lifecycle indexing
note: Sealing is opt-in (ToolLoop::with_journal_cipher, feature encryption); a person named only inside run content is not found by StepJournal::erase.
evidence: JournalEntry records RunOwner (tenant, caller, task); runs_of and erase serve access and erasure; bodies sealed and bound to key and revision. Three canaries (prompt, tool arguments, result) absent from the stored body. Live: the SQLite file held neither the prompt nor the tool's result; another key could not open the run; erase removed Alice's run.
tests: tool_loop/run_tests/journal_sealed.rs; journal store contract; tests/tool_loop_review_live.rs; tests/tool_loop_audit_live.rs

finding: Duplicate model call IDs collapse replay and action receipts
evidence: Reproduced first: an ambiguous reply ran its calls, a reused id left one receipt, two results went back under call-0-1. Now refused before any call runs (LoopError::AmbiguousCalls); generated ids are unique in the run; receipts keyed by turn and id.

finding: Tool results, accumulated history and checkpoints lack aggregate size bounds
note: Bounds are bytes, not tokens: a model's context window is not known to the loop.
evidence: Reproduced first: a 2,097,152-byte result reached the model whole. Defaults: result 1 MiB (cut, with a note), request 8 MiB (LoopError::TooLarge), checkpoint 32 MiB. Live: with a 2,048-byte limit the model was shown 2,121 of 207,018 bytes (limit plus note) and answered.

finding: Signed-card trust policy is discarded before extended-card adoption
note: Without card keys (a client not built from a signed card) the extended card is checked for shape only, as documented.
evidence: Reproduced first: an unsigned extended card declaring push notifications was adopted. The keys are kept and the extended card verified as received; unsigned and forged cards fail and push stays refused locally.

finding: Interface negotiation accepts future minors but emits fixed 1.0
evidence: The old code chose a listed 1.1 interface while every request says A2A-Version: 1.0. Selection now requires Major.Minor 1.0 (patch ignored, spec 3.6).

finding: Explicit tenant overrides can violate the selected card interface's tenant tuple
note: Opt-in: ClientBuilder::with_strict_interface_tenant(); the default keeps the documented override for gateways.
evidence: Strict mode refuses a request naming another tenant before sending (ClientError::Config) and a build that replaced the card's tenant.

finding: Release CI is a reduced duplicate of main CI and omits the configuration currently failing
note: Not yet exercised by a real tag on GitHub: the workflow steps are proven by the fail-proof harness, not by a release.
evidence: New job ci-evidence (scripts/ci_evidence.py) fails unless the newest completed push or dispatch run of ci.yml for the tagged SHA concluded success with no failed, cancelled or timed-out job; package needs it and writes and verifies release_evidence.py's manifest with the static gates run; both JSON files are attached to the release. Self-test 13 cases with three hand mutants; prove_workflow_gates_fail.py: both new steps PROVEN; whole harness 34 proven, 0 unproven.

finding: Passing semver job skips the compatibility checks relevant to migration review
note: Inventory, compile rehearsal and a SQLite data and rollback rehearsal done; PostgreSQL, the other stores, and a rolling two-version deployment were not rehearsed.
evidence: migration-inventory.md: cargo-semver-checks 0.51.0 forced to minor (11 failing lints, 39 structs newly non_exhaustive) and a public-only cargo-public-api diff (93 removed or changed items), every one named in the upgrade guide; every v0.15.0 example checked against 0.16 (4 compile unchanged, 39 error sites, all of two documented kinds); 0.15 and 0.16 binaries reading and appending each other's SQLite task and audit files, the chain verifying and every sealed actor revealed both ways.

finding: Mutation aggregation can announce all caught while individual mutant timeouts remain inconclusive
note: Verified on synthetic shard reports, not on a GitHub run.
evidence: The aggregator counted only missed.txt (a timeout-only report exited 0). It now tabulates caught, missed, timed out and unviable, lists the timeouts and fails on them (the same report exits 1; a clean one exits 0).
tests: mutants.yml aggregator step, run by hand on synthetic reports

finding: Streamed model completions globally request Connection: close
note: The handshake cost on a remote TLS endpoint was not measured.
evidence: Measured on llama.cpp 9daa0aa: llama-server closed the connection after each streamed answer (3 of 3), so the default stays; OpenAiChatModel::with_stream_connection_reuse() opts out per model.

finding: Main CI red: two mDNS discovery tests fail on stable macOS, no-default-features
note: Diagnosed, not root-caused; no test was skipped or weakened.
evidence: In run 43394485744 each test process on macOS found the other process's announcement and not its own; the same job passed at 124b70f4 with identical discovery code; on Linux 0 failures in 160 concurrent-process runs. CONJECTURED: same-process delivery between the separate announcer and browser ServiceDaemons on the macOS runner. N13's gate refuses a release while this job is red.

finding: A blocking send on a single-worker runtime could hang until the executor timeout (found by this work's live tests)
evidence: The collecting task runs the executor inline on one worker and stopped polling it while folding an event; an executor holding the audit chain lock across a store read (AuditedPolicy) waited for the fold, which waited for the lock. Located with markers and a contention backtrace (holder: AuditLog::append in the resumed run; waiter: SyncCollector::fold -> AuditedTaskStore::append_event). Unit test reproduced it first (no answer in 10 s); live approval test, whole file in one process: 5 hangs in 11 runs before (5 of the 11 carried eprintln markers; 4 runs with backtrace capture on every lock all passed and are not counted), 0 in 8 after. The live tests were then split into tool_loop_review_live.rs and tool_loop_audit_live.rs (500-line rule); the approval test now runs in a process of its own, where the hang did not occur before the fix either (6 of 6 isolated runs passed), so the unit test is the regression guard and the live file is not.

finding: Test-only applied-mark gates were keyed by an address a later manager could reuse
evidence: streaming/event_queue/manager.rs kept gates in a static keyed by Arc::as_ptr and never removed them, so a later test's manager allocated at a freed address would wait at a gate nobody opens. Keyed by a Weak now, which holds the allocation, and dead gates are pruned.

finding: N03's PostgreSQL tests wrote to the database the audit store's contract test clears and counts
note: Test-only; found by running ci.yml's test-postgres job locally, before any CI run of this branch.
evidence: audit::tests::the_postgres_store_keeps_the_contract deletes the shared database's audit tables and then asserts chains() == ["c", "other"]; the two key_lifecycle PostgreSQL tests (aa26b2b0) ran in the same process and wrote n03-<random> chains there meanwhile, so the contract test saw ["c", "n03-…", "n03-…", "other"]. Each now creates a scratch database of its own and drops it, as the subject-key store test already did; the contract's exact assertion is kept.

finding: Named deployment profiles validated at startup, with escape hatches reporting the guarantees they disable (PDF section 3)
note: Stores, authentication and (through MultiTenant) the tenant resolver are validated; audit privacy, URL/egress policy and proxy trust are not validated by any profile; the step journal, key custody and retention are reported as not verifiable at startup rather than checked.
evidence: Profile::LocalDevelopment (refused beside Production or DurableProduction) and Profile::DurableProduction (refuses no authenticator, no task store, and a task, push-config, push-outbox, halt, lease or audit store that keeps its state in this process); tenant-isolated multi-replica is DurableProduction + Production + MultiTenant. RequestHandler::profile_report() lists what build() checked, each escape hatch given and what it gives up (also logged at WARN), and what no startup check can establish. TaskStore and PushOutbox gain is_process_local (wrappers forward); SQLite stores over sqlite::memory: answer true. 28 hand mutants of the new decisions and answers, each applied with the source hash checked on restore: 27 killed at first; the survivor (an in-memory push-config store beside a card that declares push) got its test and is killed. Three of the first run's mutants did not compile (a guard that left a match non-exhaustive) and were rewritten so they did.
